source.title: Within-layer Diversity Reduces Generalization Gap
source.authors: Firas Laakom; Jenni Raitoharju; Alexandros Iosifidis; M. Gabbouj

record.file_problem: none; the supplied paper text is complete. Its title in the text is “Learning distinct features helps, provably,” differing from the metadata title.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes feature diversity and generalization bounds, but does not test or rely on any double-descent version. Its plotted results concern feature diversity or correlations with generalization gap, not test error across model size, epochs, or sample size.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 tracks feature diversity over training, not test error. Figure 2 varies sample count and reports correlations between a theoretical bound and generalization gap; it does not report whether test error rises near an interpolation threshold. Figure 3 reports diversity across depth and models, not test error versus size.
record.test_reason: The paper derives diversity-dependent Rademacher generalization bounds for two-layer networks. It never mentions double descent and reports no test-error curve over model size, epochs or sample size. Figure 2 reports only correlations between a scaled bound term and the generalization gap across training-set sizes. Figures 1 and 3 track feature diversity, not test error. The schema has no 'unrelated' option, so 'discusses' is the closest fit. The only touchpoint is the intro's classical statement that over-parameterized networks tend to overfit, asserted without test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that more distinct hidden-layer features give tighter generalization bounds, extend this to deeper nets and other losses, and report empirical bound-gap correlations above 0.99. They also conjecture that SGD implicitly optimizes feature diversity. They say nothing about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies feature diversity and generalization bounds; it does not apply a double-descent method.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST two-layer nets (hidden sizes 128/256/512), a scaled bound term (C5^2 - dmin^2)/sqrt(N) correlates with the generalization gap across training-set sizes: 0.9948, 0.9939, 0.9953.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A feature-diversity-dependent bound tracks the generalization gap across training-set sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Final last-hidden-layer diversity rises with depth (1-12) for FCN-256/512/1024 on MNIST. Diversity also rises during SGD training of ResNets on CIFAR10 and ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD implicitly increases intermediate-feature diversity, and diversity increases with depth.

record.problems: The paper does not report claim-relevant double-descent outcomes. Figure 2 provides correlations rather than the underlying test-error trend, and its caption describes the gap as train error minus test error while the main text describes it as test error minus train error.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1’s diversity-over-epochs results and Figure 3’s diversity-versus-depth/model results are not rows: neither measures test error or double descent.

untested.parts: All: no test error versus model size; Fig 3 varies depth but reports only diversity.
All: Figs 1 and 3 track diversity over epochs, not test error.
All: Fig 2 varies sample size but reports only the gap-bound correlation, with no interpolation-threshold analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The record's title mismatch note and the gap-sign inconsistency (Fig 2 caption says train minus test; Section 5 says test minus train) are accurate. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test-error curve and peak near interpolation.
Test-error increase with more training samples near interpolation.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
Noise, regularization, and multiple-peak effects on double descent.
Whether effective parameter counting converts second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
